 Here’s the Average Social Security Benefit Once 2027’s 3.6% COLA Comes Through
 Maurie Backman Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:52 PM PST 4 min read Quick Read 
 A 3.6% COLA in 2027 lifts the average monthly Social Security retirement benefit from about $2,095 to roughly $2,170, a $75 raise. 
 Higher Medicare Part B premiums and persistent inflation could erode the raise, leaving seniors who rely solely on benefits still struggling. 
 Seniors can stretch their income by working part-time, cutting expenses like cars and subscriptions, or relocating to cheaper areas, since benefits don't change by location.

 Many seniors today rely heavily on Social Security for income. Thankfully, people who can't live without those benefits just got some good news. 
 J.J. Gouin / Shutterstock.com Social Security benefits are getting a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment, or COLA, in 2027. That increase should raise the average monthly benefit quite substantially. But that doesn't mean that seniors who live on Social Security alone won't struggle. 
 The average benefit is climbing 
 The Social Security Administration puts the average monthly benefit at $2,095 before the upcoming 3.6% COLA is applied. Once that COLA comes through, the average monthly retirement benefit should increase to $2,170. 
 A $75 monthly raise might seem like a lifeline at first. But it's not a complete solution for those who are struggling today. 
 First of all, if the cost of Medicare Part B rises in 2027, seniors who are enrolled will lose a chunk of their COLA. That's because Part B premiums are automatically deducted from Social Security benefits.

 Also, if living costs continue to rise in 2027, a 3.6% COLA may not help seniors keep up. We don't know what's in store for inflation, but in 2026, it rose faster than many people expected in the wake of the Middle East conflict. It would be naive to assume that inflation will slow down in the new year, even with the Federal Reserve trying to tame it with interest rate hikes. 
 How to improve your finances in 2027 
 Story Continues If you're on Social Security and collect an average benefit, you may be looking forward to an additional $75 a month, give or take. But you shouldn't expect your upcoming raise to substantially improve your financial picture. 
 If it's a struggle today to cover your costs, you need a more comprehensive plan for 2027. That could include going back to work in some capacity to boost your income and reducing expenses. 
 If it's not possible to shed large expenses, start with small ones. Strategically shopping for food and canceling one subscription you can do without could give you more breathing room. And if you can shed larger expenses, it could make a big difference. 
 Getting rid of a car, for example, could free up hundreds of dollars a month in insurance, maintenance, and fuel costs. It's a change worth exploring if you live in a walkable city and don't have mobility issues. 
 At the same time, you may want to consider moving to a less expensive part of the country if the area you're in currently has higher costs. Social Security will pay you the same monthly benefit no matter where you live. And if those benefits are your only source of retirement income, even if you move to a state where Social Security is taxed, you'll likely qualify for an exemption, allowing you to keep your benefits in full. 
 All told, the average Social Security benefit should get a nice boost once the upcoming 3.6% COLA arrives. But don't expect that raise to be enough to change your finances for the better. Instead, take matters into your own hands so you don't keep struggling.
